assignments.node_id: מי שיש לו דעת ויודע שהכל בהשגחה מהשם יתברך
assignments.reason: This node describes the person who possesses da'at and recognizes that everything comes from Hashem's hashgacha. Its essential nature is the state of hashgacha-awareness — the core spiritual quality of Package 1. Da'at here is the faculty through which one grasps hashgacha, and the Torah identifies this awareness as the root that eliminates all suffering. The node belongs with השגחה, תפלה, and גדול as another expression of the hashgacha domain.

assignments.node_id: אין לו שום יסורין, ואינו מרגיש שום צער
assignments.reason: Freedom from suffering and pain. Despite describing a state regarding יסורין, the essential nature of this node is the positive condition of being under hashgacha — the Torah presents this as the defining characteristic of one who has hashgacha-awareness. It is not an independent concept of 'suffering' (which would be evil-domain) but rather the holy state where suffering is nullified. It belongs in Package 1 as a manifestation of what hashgacha produces in a person's experience.

assignments.node_id: שיודע בדעת ברור שהכל בהשגחה מהשם יתברך
assignments.reason: Clear knowledge (da'at barur) that everything is from Hashem's hashgacha. This is essentially the same domain as the first node — hashgacha-awareness — with emphasis on the clarity of the knowledge. Its essential nature is da'at-of-hashgacha, firmly within the good-polarity hashgacha domain of Package 1.

assignments.node_id: על כן בהכרח מרגיש היסורים בעת הפרוד, אף־על־פי־כן היסורים קלים מאד ונוחים להתקבל
assignments.reason: Suffering at the time of the soul's separation from the body that is nevertheless light and easy to bear. The Torah specifies that this lightening occurs because of hashgacha-awareness (da'at barur). The essential nature of this node is not 'suffering' per se but the hashgacha-mitigated experience — even unavoidable physical pain becomes bearable through da'at. This places it squarely in the hashgacha domain of Package 1, on the good side.

assignments.node_id: שאר מיני צער ויסורין שאין מרגישין כלל כשיש לו דעת
assignments.reason: Other types of pain and suffering that are not felt at all when one has da'at. Like the previous nodes, the essential nature here is the nullification of suffering through hashgacha-awareness. The Torah presents this as the stronger case (kal va-chomer): these sufferings vanish entirely under da'at. The node describes the complete efficacy of hashgacha and belongs in Package 1.
